chunk_map.heading: A hypothesis can meet a working slice the same day

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L8: "It only works if the bet comes first." closest to unresolved; "It" binds to the same-day test in L6 and "the bet" is named in L4 ("Write the bet in the morning"), both inside the chunk. Harm (unresolvable referent) absent.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.na_reason: no 'the X you did/saw' backward reference

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.

rules_evaluated.evidence: L4-8: three paragraphs each carry a claim; closest to thin is L6 "A test that used to wait for a sprint can now happen before the idea has gone cold." but it is a full self-carrying claim.
L1 header "A hypothesis can meet a working slice the same day" is what L4-L6 say; L8 qualifier (bet first) does not contradict it, header uses "can".

No "Not X. Not Y. Z.", no triple anaphora, no superlative, no number+retraction, no verb triplet. Closest: L4 "a clickable prototype, a landing-page variant or a first analytics query" is a concrete noun list, not a verb triplet or abstraction stack.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: closest: L4 "bet" and "slice" are ordinary product vocabulary, not repo dialect; no beat/mood/compendium/surface-as-noun in body L1-9.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -c "\*\*" over body L1-9 → 0; no bold at all, inside the budget.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Presence precedes content — verify against the composed deck, not long-read.
rules_evaluated.na_reason: slide file inlined into a lecture by include; no phase-less prose section

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: In-deck links work now; whether they EARN their place is open.

Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: lecture-shaped slide; L1 header is a claim ("A hypothesis can meet a working slice the same day"), not a label.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A bullet earns its slot or dies — three classes that read as rigour and carry nothing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: closest: L6 "A test that used to wait for a sprint can now happen before the idea has gone cold." could read as restating L4, but adds the consequence (the sprint wait removed); L8 adds the condition (bet first). No doctrine restatement, design commentary or kicker.
